title: H5160 (122nd General Assembly): Firearms and ammo

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2018-03-20; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess122_2017-2018/prever/5160_20180320.htm (LegiScan doc 1765327))
provenance.note: Introduced text, as filed; no passage vote recorded in the data. Struck: 'violent crime, as defined by Section 16-1-60, that is classified as a felony offense' and the fine of $2,000/5 years.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (Section 16-23-500(A)): It is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of a crime punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of more than one year to possess, ship, transport, or receive a firearm or ammunition within this State.
SECTION 1 (Section 16-23-500(B)): A person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction: (1) for a first offense, must be imprisoned not more than ten years; (2) for a second offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of five years, but not more than thirty years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted; and (3) for a third offense or subsequent offense, must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum of fifteen years, but not more than thirty years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted.
SECTION 1 (Section 16-23-500(E)): A prior offense for purposes of this section means any conviction related to the possession, shipping, transporting, or receiving of a firearm or ammunition in this State, another state, or in violation of federal law.
